entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Diwakar Nath Shukla - Advocate for the appellant  Shri Vivek Agrawal - Advocate for respondents No.1 to  ORDER This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the award dated 14.07.2023 passed by the Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Betul, in MACC No.35/2020, whereby an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-
has been awarded to the respondents/claimants for the death of Nitin Pawar.
2.
Brief facts of the case are that on 31.03.2018, deceased Nitin Pawar alongwith Digraj Suryawanshi was going from Pathakheda to Jamsawali Temple on a motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-48/MQ- 5019.
As they reached Seoni, near petrol pump due to mechanical failure the motorcycle got imbalanced and dashed against the divider.
As a result, deceased alongwith motorcycle fell on the road and received severe injuries on his head, hand, leg and other parts of the body.
The deceased was taken to CHC Pandhurna, wherefrom he was referred to Nagpur hospital.
On NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43209 2 MA-6017-2023 09.04.2018 the deceased succumbed to injuries.
It was stated that at the time of accident the deceased was hale and hearty and was earning Rs.3,000/- per month.
Accordingly, a claim petition seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.13,68,000/- was preferred before the Claims Tribunal.

3. The non-applicant no.1 while accepting the averments of the claim partially stated that the accident was not caused by the said vehicle and a false case has been prepared for claiming the compensation amount; the vehicle in question was insured by the insurance company on the alleged date of accident; he never given the said motorcycle to any Nitin Pawar for riding and no accident have ever been occurred by said vehicle, the death of deceased was caused due to some other reason.

The non-applicant no.2/insurance company filed reply denying the averments made in the claim National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Tikaram Pawar on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27212440/
1 petition and stated that there was breach of policy conditions and the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of deceased himself; there was no mechanical failure and in fact the claim application is not acceptable, therefore, the claim deserves to be dismissed.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Tikaram Pawar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the Tribunal failed to appreciate the aforesaid aspect and erroneously overlooked the breach of policy and conditions and thereby fastened the liability on the insurance company to pay the compensation and awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-/ against appellant/insurance Co.

Hence, this misc. appeal has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company contending that the compensation awarded is exorbitant, excessive and not in accordance with the settled principles of law.

4. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and upon careful NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:43209 3 MA-6017-2023 perusal of the record, it is upheld that no cogent and reliable evidence has been submitted to establish any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

5. Counsel for respondent submitted that the matter is fully covered by the judgment dated 07.01.2020 passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramkhiladi and Anr. vs. The United India Insurance Company and Anr. (Civil Appeal No.9393/2019), whereby Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the provision of Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act cannot be said to have any application with regard to an accident wherein the owner of the motor vehicle himself is involved.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi and Anr. vs. The United India Insurance Company and Anr. (Civil Appeal No.9393/2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is ultimately concluded that the liability under Section 163-A of the Act is on the owner of the vehicle as a person cannot be both, a claimant as also a recipient and therefore, the heirs of the owner could not have maintained the claim in terms of Section 163-A of the Act.
It is further observed that, for the said purpose, only the terms of the contract of insurance could be taken recourse to.

In the recent decision of this Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Ashalata Bhowmik (2018) 9 SCC 801, it is specifically held by this Court that the parties shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Ashalata Bhowmik (2018) 9 SCC 801
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, as per the contract of insurance, the insurance company shall be liable to pay the compensation to a third party and not to the owner, except to the extent of Rs.1 Lakh as observed hereinabove.

6. In view of the foregoing discussion, it is apparent that the learned Tribunal has rightly held that the alleged breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy was not established on the basis of the material available NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:43209 4 MA-6017-2023 on record.
Accordingly, the Insurance Company cannot be exonerated from its contractual liability.
The finding recorded by the Tribunal are based on proper appreciation of evidence and are neither perverse nor contrary to law.
Hence, no interference is called for by this Court in this appeal.
The present appeal being devoid of any substance is hereby dismissed.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE rv National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Tikaram Pawar on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27212440/
